content: TAO (arXiv 2510.16028, 'Tolerance-Aware Optimistic Verification for Floating-Point Neural Networks'): explicitly frames the security tension this milestone faces -- accepting outputs within a tolerance region beyond simple bitwise equality reopens exactly the attack surface a strict hash was meant to close (model swaps, quantization downgrades, graph rewrites that fall inside a loose tolerance band). TAO's answer is per-operator IEEE-754 worst-case bounds combined with tight empirically-calibrated percentile profiles per hardware class, rather than one flat global tolerance -- a global 'round to N decimal places' cutover that is loose enough to absorb worst-case cross-hardware noise is, by construction, also loose enough to absorb a meaningfully-wrong or substituted result if that result's error happens to land inside the same band.
